title: Dissent by department
question: Whose contracts, leases and grants draw a no vote most often?
finding: Among the 27 departments with 20 or more files, the share with a no vote is highest for Controller (10 of 35, 28.6%); Public Library (5 of 22, 22.7%); Sheriff (5 of 24, 20.8%); Economic and Workforce Development (3 of 40, 7.5%). 9 of the 27 had none at all, among them Office of Contract Administration (130 files), Port (94 files), District Attorney (76 files), City Administrator (34 files). The numbers are small: 67 files with a no across those departments, 27 of them part of a same-day list. What sets the top of the list apart is a handful of recurring items (Controller: 8 of its 10 are certifications that a service can be done by a private contractor for less than by City employees; Public Library: 3 of its 5 name one organization, Friends of the San Francisco Public Library; Sheriff: 3 of its 5 name one organization, San Francisco Pretrial Diversion Project).
how: The department is the one the title names (“authorizing the Department of Public Health to …”), mapped to the City’s department names by the same table that built the file list. Files whose title names no department, and appropriation ordinances, are shown in rows of their own. The other columns are as on the screen by kind of file.
limits: A unanimous vote is the ordinary result and no sign of anything wrong. 3,419 of the 3,483 files were recommended by a committee before the Board voted, 900 accept a grant or gift, and 1,104 amend or extend an agreement already in place. Of the 770 files of $10 million or more introduced since 2019, 650 carry a report by the Board’s Budget and Legislative Analyst among their attachments, so a vote with no dissent can follow written scrutiny at the committee stage. A no vote is ordinary; the vote pages give no reasons, and dissent can reflect a disagreement about policy or the budget rather than doubt about the organization named in the file. A department with more disputed programmes will show more no votes whatever the merits of its contractors. Dollar figures are the totals named in file titles: an agreement amended twice is counted at each new total, rent and accepted grants are money coming to the City as well as money going out, and budget ordinances name no single figure, so a sum of title dollars measures what the titles name, not money spent. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. 1 money file (160358) whose final passage is among them is left out of the counts, and none is counted as unanimous. 104 of the final votes counted here were read from the minutes. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
